title: Flow CAM 8000 Operation Protocol
author: Brittany N Zepernick
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.74qhqvw
materials: No software prompt is needed to install the flow cell. The top of the flow cell is indicated with paint and also where the tiny etching is denoting its size and manufacturing details.
Open the FlowCam software (visual spreadsheet) and select set-up, pump, and make sure the correct syringe size is listed in the syringe size box.
Auto-image: images every particle, fluorescent and non-fluorescent.
Trigger: images every fluorescent particle only.

steps.title: Power on FlowCAM
steps.instruction: Turn the fan ON using the switch on the back, press the circular power button on the top right, and power on the monitor. Remember to shut down the FlowCAM after use.

steps.title: Select objective and accessories
steps.instruction: Choose objective, flow cell, and syringe based on sample type: 20× objective with its designated flow cell and syringe for cyanobacteria; 10× objective for larger phytoplankton (diatoms, dinoflagellates, green algae). Do not mix sizes.

steps.title: Install and verify objective
steps.instruction: Click **Setup → Install Objective**, clean the objective lens with a lens wipe, screw it into the fitting on the objective stage, check the magnification box on the screen, and click OK.

steps.title: Assemble flow‑cell tubing
steps.instruction: Attach tubing pieces and position the flow cell as follows:

substeps.instruction: Screw the black (lower silicone) tubing into the bottom of the flow cell (do not overtighten).
Fit the beige tubing into the top inlet port and tighten.
Place the tubing into the fluid‑position sensor (black fitting under the sample port) and seat the flow cell in its retainer cavity without scratching.
Insert the flow‑cell retainer piece until flush and tighten the thumb screws (avoid overtightening).
Ensure the etched face of the flow cell points toward you.
Fit the lower silicone tubing end over the syringe port, keeping it straight and untwisted.

steps.title: Load new syringe
steps.instruction: Replace the syringe and set its plunger:

substeps.instruction: Click **Setup → Pump → Change Flow Cell**, turn the plunger‑lock screw counter‑clockwise three times, and press OK (plunger will be pulled down).
Turn the old syringe counter‑clockwise, remove it, and press OK.
Screw in a new syringe, pull the plunger down until it is flush with the pump, and press OK.
Tighten the plunger screw‑lock clockwise, press OK, select the installed syringe size, and press OK.

steps.title: Prepare cleaning solutions
steps.instruction: Fill the cleaner receptacle with 2 % citra‑jet, fill the rinse receptacle with Milli‑Q water, and empty the waste receptacle.

steps.title: Run cleaning cycle
steps.instruction: Perform cleaning and rinsing before and after each use:

substeps.instruction: Click **Clean/Rinse**, check **Run at end of analysis** (unless optimizing a new sample).
If processing many samples, select **Manually Prime** and prime with water or 2 % citra‑jet at 2.0 mL/min.
Verify that **Number of cycles to perform** is set to 2 mL/min and **Pump Type** is “C80 Syringe”.
Confirm cleaning by observing liquid flow, bubbles, and clicking sounds.

If cleaning fails, fill the syringe with air, disconnect the two lines to the right of the flow cell, attach the syringe to the second opening, push air, re‑attach the white connections, and retry cleaning.

steps.title: Set up focus view
steps.instruction: Click **Setup/Focus** to display a live camera view and the pump control box.

steps.title: Adjust acceptable region
steps.instruction: Position the red acceptable‑region lines just inside the flow‑cell edges:

substeps.instruction: Coarse adjustment: turn the silver knob on the pi stage to center the lines.
Fine adjustment: click **Setup → Capture**, modify the left/right numeric values, and click **Apply**.

steps.title: Prepare bead solution
steps.instruction: Create a bead mixture for autofocus:

substeps.instruction: Insert a pipette tip, fill it with Milli‑Q water and the appropriate bead solution (15 mm or 100 mm beads; for both 20× and 10× objectives use 3 drops of 15 mm beads).
Shake well, add the beads, then add 1 mL Milli‑Q water and pump the tip to mix thoroughly.
Set the pump flow rate to 2.00 mL/min and click **Set**.

steps.title: Prime flow cell with beads
steps.instruction: Click **Start Pump** and wait until the live view shows no droplets and beads appear (water filling the flow cell). Then click **Pause Pump** to stop and remove bubbles or low bead concentration.

steps.title: Auto‑focus the system
steps.instruction: Perform autofocus:

substeps.instruction: Click **Auto‑focus**, press **Next**, confirm the correct objective, flow cell, and syringe, and press **Next** again.
Select **Best Focus Image**; the system will focus automatically and display a collage of beads, indicating success or failure.

steps.title: Clear beads after focus
steps.instruction: Remove residual beads and verify region alignment:

substeps.instruction: Click **OK** to aspirate remaining lines and remove the pipette tip.
Click **Setup → Focus → Mode**, then pump 1–2 mL Milli‑Q at 2 mL/min to flush the flow cell.
Re‑check the red acceptable‑region lines and adjust via **Capture → Acceptable Region** if needed.

steps.title: Create or load context file
steps.instruction: Define imaging settings for the sample:

substeps.instruction: Click **Context**, then **Load**.
For a new context: choose **Save Context File As**, name the file, and set stop conditions (cell count, volume, time, or “sample volume aspirated”).
Set Fluorescent Measurement Settings: Minimum 3.74, Maximum 6.84, enable **Noise Threshold Multiplier**, set **Gain** to 10.
To load an existing context: choose **Load a Context File**.

steps.title: Set capture parameters
steps.instruction: Adjust image‑capture options:

substeps.instruction: Distance to nearest neighbor: 0 for very concentrated samples, 1 for branching/long specimens.
Close holes: 0 for colored samples, ≥1 for clear samples.
Collage Image Border: set to 2.
Select **Save Collage Image**, **Save Binary Image**, and (for new contexts) **Save Raw Camera Images**.
Check **Rolling Calibration**.
Select **Both Dark and Light Pixels** for phytoplankton; set both thresholds to 20 and adjust as needed.

steps.title: Configure fluidics
steps.instruction: Enter sample and flow‑rate information:

substeps.instruction: Confirm the correct flow cell is selected.
Enter the sample volume and choose a flow rate appropriate for the objective (see the FlowCam 8000 Series Visual Spreadsheet Configuration Optimization Guide).
Target overall efficiency ≈70 % and enable manual prime with the sample.
Enable dilution, set ratio to 1, and click **Find Ratio**; if the sample is colored, dilute 10‑fold or 100‑fold in Milli‑Q or appropriate media.

steps.title: Select filter size
steps.instruction: Set filter limits and choose filter based on objective:

substeps.instruction: Click **ABD**, set Minimum (e.g., 2) and Maximum (e.g., 10000) values according to expected particle size.
Use a 100 µm filter for 10× objective and a 50 µm filter for 20× objective.

steps.title: Prepare and load sample
steps.instruction: Filter, dilute, and load the sample into a pipette tip:

substeps.instruction: Apply the previously determined filter and dilution.
Load the diluted sample into the pipette tip.

steps.title: Enter dilution for PPUI
steps.instruction: Record the dilution factor in the fluidics window so the software can calculate particles per used image (PPUI). Aim for PPUI 1–1.2; if PPUI > 2, dilute further (start with 1:10).

steps.title: Acquire data
steps.instruction: Start image acquisition:

substeps.instruction: With the sample in the pipette tip, click **Auto‑image** (all detectable objects) or **Trigger mode** (fluorescent particles only).
Set the stop condition (time, cell number, volume, etc.).
For new samples, enable **Collect Raw Image** to allow post‑run parameter adjustments.

steps.title: Review and clean images
steps.instruction: Post‑run image handling:

substeps.instruction: Click **Show All** to view the scatterplot of imaged cells.
Click **Open View** to examine individual images; delete bubbles, irregular particles, or unwanted images.
If binary overlay shows unshaded regions, increase the **Close holes** value.

steps.title: Export results
steps.instruction: Save and export data to an Excel sheet or library as needed.

steps.title: Final cleaning after runs
steps.instruction: Perform a final clean‑rinse cycle and remove the pipette tip:

substeps.instruction: Go to **Setup → Pump Controls**, select **Clean and Rinse**, set for 2 cycles, and start.
Remove the pipette tip before the cleaning begins.
